question.problem:
Consider the function $y=\frac{(x+6)^{3}{cos}^{4}⁡x}{(x-1)^{7}}.$  The derivative of this function is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=-\frac{(x+6)^{2}{cos}^{3}⁡x}{(x-1)^{8}}((ax+45)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+(4{x}^{2}+bx+c)\operatorname{sin}⁡x).
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=\frac{(x+6)^{3}{cos}^{4}⁡x}{(x-1)^{7}}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the product, quotient, and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{(x+6)^{3}{cos}^{4}⁡x}{(x-1)^{7}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((x+6)^{3})+\operatorname{ln}⁡({cos}^{4}⁡x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡((x-1)^{7}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+6)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+6)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-1)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =3\cdot \frac{1}{x+6}+4\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-7\cdot \frac{1}{x-1} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{3}{x+6}-4\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{7}{x-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{3}{x+6}-4\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{7}{x-1})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\frac{(x+6)^{3}{cos}^{4}⁡x}{(x-1)^{7}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{(x+6)^{3}{cos}^{4}⁡x}{(x-1)^{7}}(\frac{3}{x+6}-4\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{7}{x-1}) \\  & =\frac{(x+6)^{3}{cos}^{4}⁡x}{(x-1)^{7}}(\frac{3(x-1)-4\operatorname{tan}⁡x(x+6)(x-1)-7(x+6)}{(x+6)(x-1)}) \\  & =\frac{(x+6)^{3}{cos}^{4}⁡x}{(x-1)^{7}}(\frac{-4x-45-4\operatorname{tan}⁡x({x}^{2}+5x-6)}{(x+6)(x-1)}) \\  & =-\frac{(x+6)^{2}{cos}^{4}⁡x}{(x-1)^{8}}(4x+45+4\operatorname{tan}⁡x({x}^{2}+5x-6)) \\  & =-\frac{(x+6)^{2}{cos}^{3}⁡x}{(x-1)^{8}}((4x+45)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4\operatorname{tan}⁡x({x}^{2}+5x-6)\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =-\frac{(x+6)^{2}{cos}^{3}⁡x}{(x-1)^{8}}((4x+45)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x(4{x}^{2}+20x-24))\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
a+b+c=4+20+(-24)=0.
$$
